## Historical audit — S0120

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/sceneevolve_cli/C1/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL lines in this file. The supplied observations contain complete lines, not split observations; their displayed ranges are `[0, length)`.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — line 1 | The task requested an editable reconstruction of a single indoor RGB image, including viewpoint, architecture, furniture, materials and occlusions. The student’s kitchen-showroom interpretation is an inference from the image, not independently verified here. |
| Initial build — lines 3–5 | The student generated and executed a nonempty SceneAct program with multiple grouped objects: architecture, posts, cabinets, ovens, island, sink, faucet, hood and kettle. It specified procedural wood and stone-like textures, metallic settings, camera and lights. Composite parts were grouped and positioned; actual physical contact or correct connections were not independently checked. Blender reported `ok: true` and saved a render and scene. |
| First revision — lines 8, 10–12 | The harness supplied the first render and requested comparison. The student diagnosed a wall blocking the view, then moved the wall, changed camera aim and lens, and lengthened the hood. Step 2 executed successfully. The blocking diagnosis is the student’s observation, not independent image verification. |
| Second revision — lines 15, 17–19 | After receiving step 2’s render, the student described excessive visible island depth, pale cabinets and an overly tall hood. It lowered the camera, darkened materials and illumination, shortened the hood, and repositioned or widened rear elements. Step 3 executed successfully and produced a render. These are observed changes, not proof they improved the match. |
| Selection — lines 22–25 | With no executions remaining, the harness asked for the strongest of the three renders; the student returned `SELECT 3`, and a selection event recorded step 3. All three execution results reported success, but no independent visual or geometric score is supplied. |

**Teacher and autonomy.** No teacher message, teacher diagnosis, proposed teacher update, or adoption of teacher advice appears in this student trajectory. The actual inputs were the initial system/task instructions and harness render-and-review prompts; the student’s subsequent revisions show use of the review cycle, not receipt of separate teacher feedback. The recorded CLI sessions report zero tool calls; exploration consisted of student-authored scene variants executed by the harness, rather than external browsing or filesystem exploration (lines 2, 9, 16, 23).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** This is a formal execution and selection success, not independently established reconstruction success or partial correctness. The images themselves are not visible in the supplied text, so object presence in the reference, pose and placement, material appearance, part connections, camera alignment, lighting quality and final render fidelity remain unverified. The student’s obstruction and lighting diagnoses remain hypotheses. No algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption is reported.

**Lessons.** Transferably, render feedback enabled successive, testable changes to occlusion, framing and illumination; execution success alone did not establish visual fidelity. The specific wall position, hood dimensions, kitchen layout and lighting values are task-specific. Whether step 3 was genuinely the strongest match remains unresolved.
